theory.what: Hub connecting multiple VPCs and on-premises through single gateway.
theory.why: Without TGW, connecting 10 VPCs needs 45 peering connections.
theory.how: Architecture: TGW as regional router, VPC attachments, route tables, cross-region peering.
theory.when: Use when connecting 3+ VPCs or need centralized routing.

theory.what: Stateless subnet-level firewalls. Must allow return traffic explicitly.
theory.why: Additional defense layer beyond Security Groups.
theory.how: Stateless, rule numbering, explicit deny, subnet-level. Must allow ephemeral ports for return traffic.
theory.when: Use as second layer. Keep rules simple.
theory.configuration:
# Allow HTTPS + return traffic
Inbound: 100 ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0
Outbound: 100 ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0

theory.what: Global VPC with regional subnets — no peering needed between regions.
theory.how: Differences: Global VPC, priority-based firewall rules, Shared VPC, Private Google Access.
theory.when: Use for global applications and multi-region deployments.

theory.what: Distributes traffic across instances for HA and scalability.
theory.why: Prevents single points of failure and enables horizontal scaling.
theory.how: Types: ALB (Layer 7, HTTP), NLB (Layer 4, TCP/UDP). Features: health checks, auto-scaling, SSL termination.
theory.when: Use ALB for web apps, NLB for non-HTTP.

theory.what: Connects two VPCs for private communication without internet.
theory.why: Enables shared services and cross-account access.
theory.how: Non-transitive, no CIDR overlap, cross-account supported, route table entries required both sides.
theory.when: Use for simple 2-VPC connections. Use TGW for 3+.
